name: へぎそば 地酒処 こんごう庵 神保町店
address_ja: 〒101-0051 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-18-1 千石屋ビル1F
cuisine: Niigata hegi-soba and Echigo sake on Yasukuni-dōri — funori-bound soba fanned across a cedar hegi tray (¥830 a portion), tare-katsu and tempura donburi sets at ¥980–¥1,050 for lunch, ¥4,000–¥5,000 a head at night with the sake list
neighborhood: Kanda-Jimbōchō 1-chōme, ground floor of the Sengokuya Building on Yasukuni-dōri — 119 m (2 min) from Jimbōchō Station on the Toei Shinjuku, Toei Mita and Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon lines
gf_detail: Not a gluten-free proposition, despite an interesting noodle. The shop's own copy says the hegi-soba is bound with 布海苔 (funori, a seaweed) rather than wheat — 「つなぎに布海苔を使用しているため、滑らかな喉ごし」 — which is the traditional Uonuma method, but nowhere does the shop claim the noodle is wheat-free, and hegi-soba is sold as a texture, not as an allergy product. Everything around it is wheat: the そばつゆ is ordinary wheat soy sauce, the best-selling lunch sets are 天丼 (tempura) and タレカツ丼 (flour-and-panko breaded pork in a soy tare), and both come out of the same fryer as the かき揚げ and 天ざる. A celiac has nothing safe to order here and no protocol to ask about.
vegan_detail: Nothing published. This is a Niigata izakaya built around 直送 seafood, 栃尾の油揚げ, tempura and tare-katsu, and the soba tsuyu is a bonito dashi like every soba shop's. The banquet courses are described as お造り (sashimi) plus seasonal tempura, finished with soba. A vegan would be constructing a meal out of side dishes and would have to establish the dashi question in Japanese first; the shop makes no vegetarian claim.

roles: 株式会社こんごう庵 (Kongōan Co.) — operator of three Tokyo hegi-soba shops: 神保町, 御徒町, 湯島
chef_bio.origin: Niigata Prefecture — the noodles, the seafood and the sake are all sourced from there
chef_bio.background: Kongōan is a small Tokyo group rather than one owner-chef's shop: three branches within a mile of each other (Jimbōchō, Okachimachi, Yushima) trading on a single Niigata theme, plus a roadside 峠の茶屋 こんごう庵 in Tagami, Minamikanbara-gun, Niigata, and a Noborito branch in Kanagawa that has since closed. The Jimbōchō shop's whole identity is へぎそば — a Uonuma speciality in which the buckwheat is bound with 布海苔 (funori seaweed) instead of wheat flour and served in one-mouthful coils fanned across a 'hegi', a shallow cedar box. The shop says the soba arrives from Niigata daily; it buys its vegetables from a named Niigata greengrocer, 八百屋石田屋, and its fish direct from Niigata ports. The sake list is deliberately all-Niigata and rotated monthly, with a nine-sake tasting built into the banquet course. Fifty-two seats, one 4–7 person tatami private room, all non-smoking, cards and IC accepted, English menu available — and, unusually for a soba shop, children are not admitted. No individual chef or founder is named in any public source; the group's corporate site (kongouan.jp) is a JavaScript shell that publishes no company history.
chef_bio.specialty: 新潟名物へぎそば ¥830 a portion, fanned on a cedar hegi tray; ミックス天丼へぎそばセット ¥1,050; タレカツへぎそばセット ¥1,000; 越後の地酒満喫コース with nine Niigata sakes and two hours of all-you-can-drink from ¥4,500

anecdotes.text: The shop names its binder outright: 「へぎ（杉の箱）に盛り付けられたへぎそばは、つなぎに布海苔を使用しているため、滑らかな喉ごしやコシのある歯ごたえと香りをご堪能いただけます。」 It is a texture claim, not an allergy claim.
The banquet menu is explicitly a Niigata supply chain: fish direct from Niigata ports, vegetables from the greengrocer 石田屋, 栃尾の油揚げ, and the soba to finish.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog's listing gives the address (神田神保町1-18-1 千石屋ビル1F), the phone, the seat count and the funori text. The shop's own gnavi-hosted official page (kongouan1.gorp.jp) supplies the JSON-LD coordinates 35.69661936 / 139.7591025, the current hours, 52 seats, the private-room configuration, the payment methods, the English-menu flag, the no-children policy and the banquet copy. Tabelog's nationwide name search confirms three Tokyo Kongōan branches plus the Niigata teahouse and a closed Kanagawa branch. No source names an owner-chef.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One 52-seat izakaya kitchen running a deep fryer all service: 天丼, かき揚げ, 天ざる and タレカツ (flour + egg + panko breaded pork) share it. Assume shared oil, shared boards and shared soba water.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The soba tsuyu, the katsu tare and the 海鮮漬け丼 marinade are all ordinary Japanese soy sauce; no tamari or wheat-free soy sauce is advertised anywhere on the shop's own page or its Tabelog listing.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi is the base of the soba tsuyu, and the kitchen handles sashimi and pork continuously. Nothing here is prepared away from animal ingredients.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy statement published in Japanese or English. An English menu exists, which helps with reading but not with contamination.

positives.text: English menu available; fully non-smoking; VISA/Mastercard/JCB/AmEx/Diners/UnionPay plus Suica, PASMO, iD, QUICPay and PayPay.

cultural_comfort.note: An easy walk-in for a foreign visitor: 52 seats on the ground floor of the Sengokuya Building on Yasukuni-dōri, two minutes from Jimbōchō station, an English menu on file with gnavi, fully non-smoking, and every card and IC/QR payment method accepted. Lunch sets run ¥980–¥1,050 and no reservation is needed; evenings are banquet-oriented and worth booking. One thing to know before you go: the shop's own listing states 「お子様連れNG」 — children are not admitted.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Nationwide Tabelog name search for こんごう庵 returns five shops; the Jimbōchō one is 13030009 at 神田神保町1-18-1 千石屋ビル1F, 119 m from Jimbōchō Station, matching the light record exactly. Coordinates taken from the shop's own JSON-LD on its official gnavi-hosted page rather than from a geocoder. CATEGORY FLAG: filed as MOM_AND_POP, but this is one of three Tokyo branches operated by 株式会社こんごう庵 (plus a Niigata teahouse), so it is a small chain rather than a family shop. GF downgraded ask → no: the funori-bound hegi-soba is genuinely wheat-free as a technique, but the shop makes no such claim and the tsuyu, tempura and tare-katsu are unambiguous wheat.

name: 神田錦町 更科
address_ja: 〒101-0054 東京都千代田区神田錦町3-14
cuisine: A 23-seat Meiji-era sarashina soba shop that queues out the door at lunch — pale, fine-cut white soba and seasonal 変わり蕎麦 such as よもぎ切り, most bowls ¥1,000–¥1,999, open only for a two-hour lunch and an early evening sitting
neighborhood: Kanda-Nishikichō 3-chōme — 2 min from Ogawamachi (Toei Shinjuku line), 5 min from Jimbōchō (Toei Shinjuku / Toei Mita / Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon), 7 min from Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line)
hours_raw: 月～金 11:00～14:00、17:00～18:30／土 11:00～14:00　定休日：日曜・祝日　※売り切れ次第早仕舞いすることがあります（食べログ）。ウィキペディアは「午前11時 - 午後2時、午後5時 - 午後7時」、千代田区観光協会は「11:00～14:30、17:00～19:30(L.O)」と記載。閉店時刻は日により早まるため要確認。
gf_detail: No. 更科 (sarashina) is the style in which the pale inner core of the buckwheat groat — 晒粉 — is milled out and used alone; that flour has almost no binding power of its own, which is why sarashina is the one Edo soba style that always needs a wheat binder, and why the noodle comes out white rather than grey. The shop makes no gluten statement of any kind, its tsuyu is ordinary wheat soy sauce, and its menu includes 天ぷら. This is a 23-seat, 150-year-old shop with a two-hour lunch service and a queue; there is no allergy protocol here to negotiate.
vegan_detail: Nothing published. Standard Edo soba tsuyu is a katsuobushi dashi and tempura batter is egg-and-wheat. The one thing worth knowing is that sarashina houses historically build their 変わり蕎麦 by kneading plant ingredients into the white flour — よもぎ (mugwort), citrus, tea — but the noodle still arrives with a bonito dipping sauce, so a vegan would be asking for it dry. No vegetarian or vegan claim exists in any source.

chef_bio.chef_name: 堀井市朗 (Ichirō Horii), 四代目布屋丈太郎
roles: 四代目 布屋丈太郎 / owner-proprietor
五代目 堀井雄太朗 (Yūtarō Horii, b. 1997) works alongside him
Yūtarō is a founding member of 江戸神田蕎麦の会 (2001)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Nishikichō, Chiyoda-ku — the family has stood on this block since 1869
chef_bio.background: This is the oldest continuously running branch of the most famous name in Edo soba, and the family that runs it are Horiis by marriage and Nunoyas by trade name. The parent house, 麻布永坂 更科 (today 更科堀井), was founded in 1789 by 堀井清右衛門, a Shinshū cloth merchant — a 布屋, literally 'cloth shop' — who supplied bleached Shinshū linen to the Hoshina lords of Takatō and lived in their Azabu compound. His lord, having watched him cut soba, told him he would do better as a noodle maker than a draper; he hung out a sign reading 「信州更科蕎麦所 布屋太兵衛」 and kept the old trade name. For eighty years the Azabu house opened no branches at all. Then in 1869 (Meiji 2), under the sixth-generation Matsunosuke, it permitted its first: 堀井丈太郎, Matsunosuke's cousin, married the family's daughter Kane as a 婿養子 and opened 神田錦町分店 under the shop name 布屋丈太郎. Under the family's old rule a 分店 — as opposed to a mere 支店 — could only be opened by a child of the main house, which is why Nishikichō alone carries the higher title, and why the sign outside still reads 「麻布永坂分店 神田錦町 信州更科蕎麦所 布屋丈太郎」. The shop burned in the 1923 Kantō earthquake, was rebuilt in 1927, and burned again in the March 1945 firebombing of Tokyo; land had to be handed over as tax in kind afterwards, which is why the site is small. In 1941 the Azabu main house itself went under, taking most of the 'Sarashina seven' with it, and the family gathered to ask whether Nishikichō — the blood line — should now become the honke. The second-generation Kameo refused: 「店は錦町一軒だけで十分」, one shop in Nishikichō is enough, and simply took the ruined seventh-generation head of the main house into his household. That refusal is the shop's character in one sentence. The line since: 初代 堀井丈太郎 (d. 1916), 二代目 堀井亀雄 (1893–1968), 三代目 堀井松太郎 (1926–2011), 四代目 堀井市朗 (b. 1963), 五代目 堀井雄太朗 (b. 1997), who in 2001 helped found 江戸神田蕎麦の会 with the heirs of 神田まつや and かんだやぶそば. Twenty-three seats, cash-era hours, closed Sundays and holidays, and it sells out.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「商売を長く続けていればいいというだけではありません。商売が繁盛すれば必ず偽物が出てきます。平気な顔をしてウソをつく、マネをする店が出てきます。それらを一つ一つ乗り越えて本物にならなければなりません。ただし、本人の努力だけでは本物にはなれません。」 — longevity is not the point; surviving the imitators to become the real thing is, and you cannot get there on your own effort alone.
chef_bio.specialty: さらしな (white sarashina seiro), seasonal 変わり蕎麦 including よもぎ切り and the 二色せいろ that pairs it with the plain white noodle; 天ぷらそば

anecdotes.text: A 1902 Tokyo guidebook already described the Sarashina noodle as unmistakable: 「其の製法他店と全く異にして、色白くして細く、一見愛すべし」 — made quite unlike anyone else's, white and fine, and lovely at first sight — and noted that travellers were by then carrying it aboard trains to Osaka and Kobe.

When the Azabu main house collapsed in 1941 and relatives proposed that Nishikichō take over as honke, the second-generation Kameo declined and instead took in the ruined seventh-generation head of the main family.
The comedian 内海桂子 was sent to this shop as a child servant.

The trade name 布屋 is not decoration — it is the cloth business the family left in the 1780s, kept on the signboard so the descendants would not forget the straw sandals their ancestors wore as drapers.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The Japanese Wikipedia article on 神田錦町更科 is unusually well sourced — it cites 岩崎信也『蕎麦屋の系図』(Kōbunsha, 2011), 植原路郎『そば物語』(1959), the 1824 『江戸買物独案内』, the 1902 『新撰東京名所図会』 and the 1925 『食行脚 東京の巻』 — and supplies the 1869 founding, the 1789 parent-house founding, the full Horii succession with birth and death years, the earthquake and firebombing losses, the 1941 collapse of the Azabu house, the 2001 founding of 江戸神田蕎麦の会, the address 神田錦町三丁目14番 and the shop coordinates. Tabelog 13040724 independently confirms the address, phone 03-3294-3669, 23 seats, ¥1,000–¥1,999, the current hours and the Sunday/holiday closure, and photographs the signboard reading 「麻布永坂分店 神田錦町 信州更科蕎麦處 布屋丈太郎」; it dates the founding to 1887, which conflicts with Wikipedia's better-sourced 1869. Multiple 2026-dated listings (Wikipedia's last edit, Retty visit reports, Hot Pepper, the Chiyoda tourism association) show the shop trading normally.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Twenty-three seats, one soba kitchen, a tempura pan, and a board dusted in flour all service. There is no separated preparation of any kind.

Sarashina soba is the Edo style most dependent on a wheat binder: 晒粉, the milled-out white core of the groat, has essentially no viscosity of its own, which is what produces the shop's characteristic white, fine-cut noodle.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Ordinary wheat soy sauce throughout; no tamari, no wheat-free tsuyu, and no allergen statement in any source.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Edo soba tsuyu is a katsuobushi dashi. The tempura batter uses egg. Nothing is prepared away from animal ingredients.

staff_allergy_handling.text: None published. The shop has no website of its own beyond an X account, and its service window is about two hours at lunch with a queue — not a setting built for a dietary conversation.

cultural_comfort.note: A 23-seat shop that has been in the same Kanda-Nishikichō block since 1869, with no website beyond an X account, no English menu found anywhere, a hand-written seasonal board, and a lunch service of roughly two hours that ends when the soba runs out. Closed Sundays and holidays. Wonderful if you are content to point, sit at a shared table, order 「せいろ」 and eat quickly; not a place to work out a dietary question. Sources disagree on the evening close — Tabelog says 18:30, Wikipedia 19:00, the Chiyoda tourism association 20:00 — so ring 03-3294-3669 if you are coming after work.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Tabelog nationwide search for 神田錦町 更科 returns one soba shop of that name, 13040724, at 神田錦町3-14, 403 m from Jimbōchō — matching the light record. Coordinates are the shop-level figure from the Japanese Wikipedia article (35.693750 / 139.761717), which is tighter than a banchi geocode. FOUNDING-DATE CONFLICT for the reviewer: Tabelog states 創業1887, but Wikipedia — citing 岩崎信也『蕎麦屋の系図』 and contemporary Meiji sources — states 1869 (明治2年), and every secondary source found agrees on 1869. This record uses 1869. GF downgraded ask → no.

name: なかや蒲焼店
address_ja: 〒101-0051 東京都千代田区神田神保町1-32 出版クラブビル1F
cuisine: Third-generation Edo-style eel house that has fed the Jimbōchō publishing trade since 1946 — split from the back, skewered, steamed, then grilled in a tare replenished for seventy years; unadon ¥2,200, unajū ¥3,400–¥4,200, kabayaki or shirayaki ¥2,200–¥4,900, plus an evening list of liver skewers, rolled omelette and eel-bone crackers
neighborhood: Kanda-Jimbōchō 1-chōme, ground floor of the Shuppan Club Building on Sakura-dōri just north of the Jimbōchō crossing — 146 m (2 min) from Jimbōchō Station on the Toei Shinjuku, Toei Mita and Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon lines
gf_detail: Worth asking, for one specific reason. The house tare — the seventy-year 継ぎ足し sauce the shop is built on — is soy-sauce based and therefore wheat, and so is everything glazed with it. But the à-la-carte 鰻料理 list carries 白焼 (plain-grilled eel, no tare) at exactly the same prices as the kabayaki: 並 ¥2,200 / 上 ¥3,900 / 特上 ¥4,900. Shirayaki is normally eaten with wasabi and salt, which makes it the one plate in this shard a celiac could plausibly eat — if you bring your own tamari and if the kitchen will grill it clear of the tare-basted eels. Both are questions to ask, not assumptions: the shop publishes no allergen information, the same charcoal grill handles both, and a fryer runs for 揚げたて骨せんべい. Do not order anything 重, 丼, う巻き or うざく.
vegan_detail: An eel and loach specialist. There is nothing here for a vegan — even the 味玉 is an egg, the 柳川鍋風 is egg-bound, and the kitchen has no non-animal course.

roles: 三代目 (third-generation owner-griller)
有限会社なかや蒲焼店
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Jimbōchō, Chiyoda-ku — the shop has never left the neighbourhood since 1946
chef_bio.background: Nakaya opened in Shōwa 21 — 1946, in the rubble year — and has spent eight decades within a few hundred metres of the Jimbōchō crossing, first on Suzuran-dōri and now, since 1 December 2022, on the ground floor of the Shuppan Club Building on Sakura-dōri. Its trade is not tourists but the publishing houses that fill this district: editors, printers and booksellers taking the ¥2,200 unadon at noon. The one thing the shop asks you to notice is the tare, which it says has been topped up and never emptied since the founding — 「創業昭和21年。神田神保町にて絶やすことなく継ぎ足し続けたタレの味を是非一度ご賞味ください。」 Seventy years of drippings, in other words, is the recipe. The current owner is the third generation, who works in the Edo manner: 「３代目が熟練の技で１匹ずつ丁寧に捌いた鰻を串打ちし、ほどよく蒸し、丁寧に焼いた絶品の蒲焼」 — each eel split by hand from the back, skewered, steamed soft, then grilled. He also runs the shop's Instagram, posting where the day's eels came from, which is not typical of a shop this old. The 2022 move gave it high ceilings and daylight without changing the 25 seats or the price of lunch. It delivers four portions or more to nearby offices, has an English menu and English- and Chinese-speaking staff, is entirely non-smoking, and takes every card and IC payment there is. No individual's name is published in any source.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keep the tare alive and stay where the readers are.
chef_bio.specialty: うな重 ¥3,400 / 上 ¥4,200; うな丼 ¥2,200; 蒲焼 and 白焼 並 ¥2,200 / 上 ¥3,900 / 特上 ¥4,900; 鰻串 (くりから・短冊・ヒレ・かしら) ¥450 each; evening-only う巻き ¥1,000, うざく ¥2,000, うなぎのたたき ¥2,000, 揚げたて骨せんべい ¥700, 肝わさ ¥1,200

anecdotes.text: The shop's own headline is a count: 「創業昭和21年 神保町にて79年」 — seventy-nine years on the same few streets, and it marked its eightieth in 2026.
It reopened in a new building on 1 December 2022 without leaving the neighbourhood: 「2022年12月1日新店舗にてオープンしました！」
Trade press describes it as 「出版業界の胃袋を支えてきた老舗」 — the old shop that has kept the publishing industry fed.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The shop's own gnavi-hosted official page carries the 1946 founding, the 79-years-in-Jimbōchō line, the December 2022 move, the third-generation attribution, the seventy-year tare, the current hours with the irregular Saturday, 25 seats, the English menu and English/Chinese staff flags, the non-smoking policy and the full payment list. Tabelog 13266109 independently confirms the address 神田神保町1-32 出版クラブビル1F, the phone 03-3518-9095, the seat layout, the Sunday closure and the recent move north of the Jimbōchō crossing. The gnavi 鰻料理 menu page gives every à-la-carte price including 白焼. Syupo's feature marks the eightieth anniversary and describes the Edo steam-then-grill method. Tabelog's nationwide search separates this shop from the unrelated なかや 蒲焼店 浅草橋店 and from なか川蒲焼 in Shizuoka.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One charcoal grill handles both the tare-basted kabayaki and the plain shirayaki, and the tare is brushed on over the fire. Any shirayaki request has to include grilling it clear of the tare, and the shop has published no protocol for doing so.
A fryer runs in the evening for 揚げたて骨せんべい.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The house identity is a soy-sauce tare replenished continuously since 1946 — 「絶やすことなく継ぎ足し続けたタレ」. No tamari or wheat-free version is offered, and every 重, 丼 and 串 passes through it.

vegan_cross_contact.text: An eel and loach house. There is no non-animal preparation on the premises.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen statement published. Staff are recorded as speaking English and Chinese, which at least makes the shirayaki question askable across a language barrier.

positives.text: 白焼 (plain-grilled, no tare) is on the standing menu at the same three grades as the kabayaki — ¥2,200 / ¥3,900 / ¥4,900 — a genuine starting point for a wheat-avoidant diner in a way most unagi shops are not.
English menu, English- and Chinese-speaking staff, fully non-smoking, every major card plus Suica/PASMO/ICOCA/はやかけん/楽天ペイ/Alipay/PayPay.

cultural_comfort.note: Unusually easy for an eighty-year-old eel shop. It sits on the ground floor of the Shuppan Club Building on Sakura-dōri, two minutes north of the Jimbōchō crossing, in a room rebuilt in 2022 with high ceilings and daylight rather than the usual dark old-shop interior. Twenty-five seats, children welcome, entirely non-smoking, an English menu, and staff recorded as speaking English and Chinese. Lunch is 11:30–14:00 with last orders at 13:30 and the ¥2,200 unadon is the thing to order; dinner is 17:00–21:00. Closed Sundays and holidays, and Saturdays are irregular — call 03-3518-9095 before making a weekend trip.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Tabelog nationwide search for なかや蒲焼 returns three shops; this is 13266109 at 神田神保町1-32 出版クラブビル1F, 146 m from Jimbōchō — the light record's neighbourhood. Note the separate, unrelated なかや 蒲焼店 浅草橋店 (13031352) so the two are not conflated later. GF tier left at ask specifically because 白焼 is on the standing menu at ¥2,200–¥4,900; that is a real lead for a wheat-avoidant diner, not a general assurance.

name: 上野藪そば
cuisine: A four-generation, 130-year-old Yabu house in its own two-storey building beside Ameyoko — hand-cut nihachi soba eaten cold on a seiro, an oversized prawn tempura, duck in curry tsuyu, and 100% buckwheat sobagaki kneaded to order; most bowls ¥1,000–¥1,999, 85 seats, and a Tabelog そば百名店 2021 selection
neighborhood: Ueno 6-chōme, a standalone two-storey shop just off Ameyoko — 193 m from Keisei-Ueno (Keisei Main line), about 4 min from JR Ueno's Shinobazu exit and from JR Okachimachi (Yamanote / Keihin-Tōhoku), 5 min from Ueno-Hirokōji (Tokyo Metro Ginza line)

gf_detail: No, and the shop says so itself without meaning to. Its menu page states plainly 「当店の蕎麦は全て喉ごしを大切にした二八蕎麦です」 — every noodle in the building is nihachi, eight parts buckwheat to two parts wheat — and follows it with 「蕎麦粉、小麦粉は全て安全な国産材料を使用しております」, naming wheat flour as an ingredient it is proud of. The udon and kishimen are milled on the premises, the tsuyu is wheat soy sauce, and a tempura pan runs all service. The one 100%-buckwheat item is そばがき — 「１００％そば粉でご注文いただいてから練り上げます」 — but it is kneaded in a kitchen dusted with wheat flour and eaten with the same tsuyu, so it is a curiosity, not a safe order. The shop does invite allergy declarations, but only in one narrow place: the complimentary そば茶 carries the note 「アレルギーの方は、お申し出ください」, which is about buckwheat allergy, not wheat.
vegan_detail: Limited, and only around the edges. The soba itself is out: the tsuyu is a bonito dashi and the kitchen's vocabulary is dashi, egg and duck. What a vegan can actually order from the published menu is 茹で立て枝豆 (boiled edamame), きゅうりとそば味噌 (cucumber with soba miso — worth checking whether the miso is dashi-tempered), and possibly 厚揚げとうふ if it comes without a dashi broth. Everything else on the small-plate list is fish, egg or duck: 玉子とうふの酢の物, 本鮪のお刺身, 鴨のワイン煮, 穴子の柳川, 板わさ, 揚げ出しとうふ. Treat it as a place to drink with a couple of snacks, not to eat a meal.

chef_bio.chef_name: 鵜飼泰 (Yasushi Ukai), 四代目
roles: 四代目店主・代表取締役社長 (fourth-generation owner and president, since 2015)
株式会社上野やぶそば
chef_bio.origin: Ueno, Taitō-ku — the family has been on this site since 1892
chef_bio.background: The shop began in 1892 (明治25年) as 藪安, opened on this spot by 鵜飼安吉. His son 鵜飼禎次郎 took over in 1940, incorporated the business as 有限会社藪安 in 1953, and in 1972 the third generation, 鵜飼良平, renamed it 株式会社上野やぶそば. Ryōhei is the reason the name means something outside Ueno. Born in Tokyo in 1937, he trained six months each at Kanda Yabu and Namiki Yabusoba before coming home, and then spent his career teaching Edo soba-cutting rather than guarding it — founding the instructional group 鵜の会, sitting as an examiner for amateur soba-making certification, and publishing a shelf of books including 『そば屋のおやじのひとりごと ― 上野やぶそば三代目』. The state noticed: the 藍綬褒章 (Medal with Blue Ribbon) in 2003, and in 2015 the 旭日中綬章, received from the Emperor. That same year his son 鵜飼泰 became the fourth-generation owner. The name was deliberate — 「泰」 was chosen as a one-character variation on the founder 安吉's 「安」, so the fourth generation carries the first generation's character in altered form. Yasushi's own statement of the job is unsentimental: materials, equipment and technique all change over 130 years, and his duty is to use the best material available now, with the technique handed down, to make soba that tastes right for this era — 「その時代に合った美味しさを最良の素材を使い、受け継がれた技術で“そば”にする。これが私の使命です。」 What he says he actually thinks about day to day is not the noodle: 「常に心掛けている事は、第一にお客様が、そして従業員も、みんなが笑顔でいられる事」 — a good workplace makes good things, and only then can you hand them to a customer. The shop is a standalone two-storey building with 85 seats, mills its own udon and kishimen in house, and pours 白穂乃香 unfiltered draught and 菊正 みぞれ酒, a frozen sherbet of taru-zake.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「これまで１３０余年愛されてきた『上野やぶそば』が、これからの１００年間も愛される店づくりを目指します。」 — and, underneath it, that the staff's contentment is upstream of the food.
chef_bio.specialty: 天せいろう and 天ぷらそば with an oversized prawn; カレーせいろう and カレー南蛮 with duck; 鴨南せいろう; 100%-buckwheat そばがき kneaded to order; 板わさ cut thick from Odawara's 鈴廣 kamaboko with wasabi grated that morning

anecdotes.text: The third generation, Ryōhei Ukai, received the 藍綬褒章 in 2003 and the 旭日中綬章 from the Emperor in 2015 — decorations for a soba maker, earned mostly by teaching other people to cut soba.
The fourth generation was named for the first: 「『泰』の名は初代『安吉』の『安』から文字違いに付けられたもの」.
The shop traces its taste back past its own founding, to the Edo soba house 蔦屋: 「江戸時代の人気そば屋『蔦屋』の味を初代安吉から、禎次郎、良平と受け継がれ、今は私 泰へとつないで参りました。」
Its own menu page teaches the arithmetic behind the word nihachi — eight parts buckwheat to two of wheat, or alternatively the sixteen mon (2×8) that a bowl of kakesoba cost in the Edo period.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The shop's own site carries the full 沿革 — 1892 founding as 藪安 by 鵜飼安吉, 1940 succession to 禎次郎, 1953 incorporation, 1972 succession to 良平 and the rename, the 2003 and 2015 decorations, and the 2015 succession to 四代目 鵜飼泰 — plus the fourth generation's signed greeting, the complete menu with its explicit 二八 statement and domestic buckwheat/wheat sourcing line, and a month-by-month trading calendar (August and September 2026 are posted, which also confirms the shop is trading now). Tabelog 13003594 independently gives the address 上野6-9-16, the phone 03-3831-4728, 85 seats, the 1892 founding, the そば百名店 2021 selection and the same closure pattern. sobaweb.com and a club-willbe member profile supply Ryōhei Ukai's 1937 birth year, his six-month apprenticeships at Kanda Yabu and Namiki Yabusoba, his teaching work and his books; note that sobaweb dates his succession to 1961 while the shop's own 沿革 says 昭和47年 (1972), and this record follows the shop.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Every noodle in the building contains wheat by design, the udon and kishimen are made on site, and the board is dusted all service. An 85-seat, two-floor kitchen with a tempura pan and a tempura-donburi list.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Ordinary wheat soy sauce in the tsuyu; the white-dashi kishimen broth is likewise soy-based. No tamari is offered.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The tsuyu is bonito dashi and the small-plate list is built on egg, fish and duck. Even the tofu dishes (揚げ出しとうふ, 玉子とうふ) arrive in dashi or contain egg.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The only allergy line the shop publishes is attached to the complimentary buckwheat tea: 「ご来店時に、サービスで『そば茶』をお出ししております。（アレルギーの方は、お申し出ください。）」 That is a buckwheat-allergy courtesy and should not be read as a wheat protocol.

positives.text: Portion size is adjustable in both directions — 大盛り, a smaller さくら盛り, and for hot bowls a 「抜き」 with no noodles at all, the traditional way to take just the topping and the tsuyu.
Buckwheat and wheat flour are both stated to be domestically sourced, and the そばがき is 100% buckwheat kneaded to order.

cultural_comfort.note: A large, welcoming old shop rather than a forbidding one — 85 seats over two floors in its own building a minute off Ameyoko, open straight through from 11:30 to 21:00, no reservation needed except weekday evenings (phone only, from 17:00). But everything is in Japanese: the site, the menu, the seasonal board. The closure pattern is the real trap — every Wednesday plus the second and fourth Tuesday, with substitutions when a public holiday falls in the week, and on weekdays between 15:00 and 17:00 only the ground floor is open. The shop posts a month-by-month calendar on its site; check it before you go.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED and trading. Tabelog nationwide search returns 上野藪そば (13003594) in Tokyo and an unrelated えびな 上野藪そば in Atsugi, Kanagawa; this record is the Tokyo one, 193 m from Keisei-Ueno, matching the light record. The shop's own site publishes trading calendars for August and September 2026, so it is open. GF downgraded ask → no on the shop's own words: 「当店の蕎麦は全て…二八蕎麦です」 and 「蕎麦粉、小麦粉は全て安全な国産材料を使用しております」.

name: 喜乃字屋
address_ja: 〒110-0007 東京都台東区上野公園1-54 上野の森さくらテラス1F
cuisine: A soba bar on the Sakura Terrace deck beside Ueno Park — 生粉打ち soba pressed from 100% stone-milled Hokkaido buckwheat with no binder at all, about ¥1,000 with tempura by day, and by night the same counter pours French and Italian wine by the glass; open 10:00 to 23:30, cash only
neighborhood: Ueno-kōen 1-chōme, ground floor of Ueno-no-Mori Sakura Terrace on the park side of the station — 135 m from Keisei-Ueno (Keisei Main line), 1–3 min from JR Ueno's Shinobazu and Park exits
hours_raw: 10:00～23:30（ドリンクL.O.23:00、そばL.O.23:00、おつまみ・天ぷらL.O.22:30）　定休日：元旦（ほかに施設による休館日がございます）
gf_detail: The one lead in this shard worth a conversation, and still not a safe assumption. The noodle itself is unusual: 「北海道産キタワセソバの実を石臼で挽いた、つなぎ一切なし１００％蕎麦粉」 — Hokkaido Kitawase buckwheat, stone-milled in house, no binder whatsoever, pressed rather than rolled and cut. That is a wheat-free dough. Everything else in the building is not. The tsuyu is ordinary wheat soy sauce, the counter fries tempura all day (its signature is a 舞茸天 using 栃木県産の栃の木舞茸), and the shop has published nothing about 打ち粉 — the dusting flour on the board and in the noodle basket, which at some jūwari shops is wheat starch and at others buckwheat. Per the standing rule for Japan: jūwari is not gluten-free. If you want to try, the questions are (1) what the 打ち粉 is, (2) whether the soba can be boiled in fresh water, and (3) whether they will serve it dry so you can use your own tamari. Nobody here has published an answer.
vegan_detail: Nothing published. The soba dough is buckwheat and water only, which is promising, but the dipping tsuyu is a standard bonito dashi and the shop's own signature is a tempura — batter that normally contains egg — while the evening menu is a wine bar's snack list. A vegan would be asking for soba served dry with no tsuyu and would still need the batter and the frying oil ruled out. No vegetarian claim exists anywhere.

roles: operated by クマガイコーポレーション株式会社 (Kumagai Corporation), a Tokyo restaurant group in its second century
chef_bio.origin: Ueno — the shop opened on the Sakura Terrace deck on 26 April 2014
chef_bio.background: Kinojiya is a deliberate hybrid and says so: its stated concept is 「クールな生粉打ちそば、粋な角打ちワイン」 — cool kiko-uchi soba, stylish standing-bar wine. 生粉打ち (kiko-uchi) is the trade term for soba made from buckwheat flour and water alone, with no binder, and the shop is emphatic that the point is not the ratio but the grain: it buys Kitawase buckwheat from Hokkaido, mills it on a stone quern in house, then presses the dough rather than rolling and cutting it, which is how a binderless dough is usually handled. By day it works as a fast, cheap soba counter at the mouth of Ueno Park — a bowl and five pieces of tempura for around a thousand yen, which is why one Japanese food blog headlined it 「『十割そば＝高級』は、もう古い？」, is jūwari-equals-expensive out of date. Its signature tempura is 舞茸 from a named Tochigi grower, 栃の木舞茸, which local coverage describes as an Imperial Household Agency supplier. By night the same twenty-eight seats become a 角打ち wine bar with bottles imported direct from France and Italy. It sits on the terrace deck of 上野の森さくらテラス, the retail building on the park side of Ueno Station, and keeps unusually long hours for a soba shop — 10:00 to 23:30, closed only on New Year's Day and when the building shuts. It is cash only. The operating company, Kumagai Corporation, describes the concept as 「伝統と革新を感じていただける全く新しい蕎麦バル」 — a soba bar meant to be felt as both traditional and new. No chef or owner is named in any published source.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「コンセプトは『クールな生打ちそば、粋な角打ちワイン』。伝統と革新を感じていただける全く新しい蕎麦バルをお楽しみください。」 — and, on the noodle, that 生粉打ち is not about the number ten but about what happens between the grain and the mill.
chef_bio.specialty: 舞茸天せいろ with 栃木県産 栃の木舞茸; 天せいろ with a five-piece tempura assortment (pumpkin, prawn, squid, maitake); とろろ蕎麦; French and Italian wine by the glass in the evening

anecdotes.text: The shop's own line on the noodle is that pure buckwheat is a means, not a boast: 「生粉打ちと銘打つのは、単に蕎麦粉10割が良いのではなく、実から蕎麦…」 — the claim is about milling the grain, not about the number ten.
A Japanese food blog used it to argue the price stereotype is dead: 「『十割そば＝高級』は、もう古い？ 上野【喜乃字屋】が変える…」
Its signature maitake tempura uses 栃木県産の栃の木舞茸, described as an Imperial Household Agency supplier and an independently developed strain.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13167680 gives the address 上野公園1-54 上野の森さくらテラス1F, the phone 03-6803-2808, 28 seats, the 26 April 2014 opening, the 10:00–23:30 hours with staggered last orders, the New Year's Day closure, and the shop's own binderless-Kitawase description. The gnavi listing (r.gnavi.co.jp/49nxrang0000) independently confirms address, hours and seat count and adds that there is no parking. Kumagai Corporation's brand page supplies the operating company and the 「クールな生打ちそば、粋な角打ちワイン」 concept line. A Nagano-prefecture restaurant guide adds the 生粉打ち explanation; a February 2025 local-media review adds the Tochigi maitake, the cash-only policy and the walking times. The shop's own site, kinojiya.com, is a Nuxt/STUDIO single-page build whose content is not served to a non-JavaScript client — it confirms the shop exists and states 「北海道産のそばの実を使用した十割蕎麦と、フランス・イタリア直輸入のワイン提供」, but no menu, prices or allergen text could be read from it.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 28-seat counter frying tempura from opening until 22:30 alongside the soba station. Shared oil and shared work surface should be assumed.
打ち粉 — the dusting flour used on the board and in the noodle basket — is not disclosed anywhere. At jūwari shops it may be wheat starch or buckwheat; here it is simply unknown.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The そばつゆ is ordinary wheat soy sauce; no tamari or wheat-free tsuyu is advertised.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi in the tsuyu; the evening service is a wine bar with meat and cheese snacks. Nothing is prepared away from animal ingredients.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen information published on Tabelog, on gnavi or on the shop's own single-page site.

positives.text: The noodle is stated to be 100% stone-milled Hokkaido Kitawase buckwheat with no binder at all — 「つなぎ一切なし１００％蕎麦粉」 — which is rarer than the phrase '十割' usually implies and is the only wheat-free dough anywhere in this shard.

cultural_comfort.note: About as low-effort as an Ueno soba shop gets: it is on the ground-floor deck of Ueno-no-Mori Sakura Terrace, the retail building right at the park side of the station, open 10:00 to 23:30 every day but New Year's Day, twenty-eight seats, no reservation, and a bowl with tempura for about a thousand yen. Two practical warnings: it is cash only, and no English menu was found in any source — the food is easy to point at, the dietary conversation is not. No parking; the building's own closure days apply.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Tabelog nationwide search for 喜乃字屋 returns one exact match, 13167680, at 上野公園1-54 上野の森さくらテラス1F, 135 m from Keisei-Ueno — matching the light record's 「京成上野駅・桜テラス」 exactly. CATEGORY FLAG: filed as MOM_AND_POP, but it is a brand of クマガイコーポレーション株式会社, a multi-brand Tokyo restaurant group. GF left at ask rather than raised or lowered: the noodle is genuinely binderless 100% buckwheat, which is a real lead, but the 打ち粉 is undisclosed and the tsuyu and tempura are wheat — a celiac would need three questions answered first.

name: 鰻割烹 伊豆栄 本店
cuisine: The founding house of a 300-year-old Edomae eel dynasty at Ikenohata by Shinobazu Pond — Mikawa Isshiki eel split from the back, charcoal-grilled, steamed, then finished in a tare of soy and mirin with no sugar at all; unajū ¥3,960–¥6,160, shirayaki ¥6,380, eel kaiseki ¥9,900–¥22,000, and 270 seats' worth of private rooms
neighborhood: Ueno 2-chōme at Ikenohata, on the Shinobazu Pond side of the park — 3 min from Ueno-Hirokōji (Tokyo Metro Ginza line, Asakusa-side exit), Keisei-Ueno and Ueno-Okachimachi (Toei Ōedo line); 5 min from JR Ueno's Shinobazu exit, JR Okachimachi's north exit and Yushima (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line)
hours_raw: 11:00〜21:00（L.O. 料理20:15／ドリンク20:30）　定休日：年中無休（12月31日・1月1日は定休日）　※平日15:00から16:30の間は、うな重と蒲焼のみのご提供となります
gf_detail: Ask, and ask about one dish. Izuei's tare is famously short — 「材料は醤油と味醂のみ」, soy sauce and mirin only, no sugar, rested two weeks to a month — which is elegant and entirely wheat, since Japanese soy sauce is a wheat ferment by default and the shop names no tamari. Every 重, 丼 and 蒲焼 is glazed with it. What makes this worth a conversation is 白焼, plain unglazed grilled eel, on the standing menu at ¥6,380 and traditionally eaten with wasabi, salt and a little soy alongside — bring your own tamari and that is eel, salt and rice. The caveats are real: it is grilled over the same charcoal as the tare-basted eels, every kaiseki course contains a 揚物 course, and 270 seats across a multi-floor banquet house means a lot of hands. No allergen statement is published in Japanese or on the shop's English site.
vegan_detail: No. This is a 300-year-old eel house whose non-eel side is traditional Japanese kaiseki built on dashi — the shop's own copy says a head chef of forty years' standing oversees a hundred cooks across four Tokyo restaurants producing seasonal 日本料理 with 「出汁のやさしい香り」. Every course on the menu page opens with 先付・前菜 and runs through 椀物 and 煮物, all dashi-based, ending with unajū. There is no vegetarian course and no published capability for one.

chef_bio.chef_name: 土肥好美 (Yoshimi Doi), 九代目女将
roles: 九代目女将 / ninth-generation okami
代表取締役社長, 株式会社伊豆榮
chef_bio.origin: Ueno Ikenohata, Taitō-ku — the shop has stood on this spot since the reign of the eighth shogun
chef_bio.background: Izuei's own account of itself begins with a correction: today 「江戸前」 makes people think of sushi, but in the city that was still called Edo, edomae meant eel. The house was born at Ueno Ikenohata in the time of the eighth shogun Yoshimune — the 1720s–30s — as one of the flimsy 小屋掛け grill shacks that lined the pond bank where good eel could be caught. Three hundred years later it is still on that spot, and the family's own framing of that fact is a list of things that should have ended it: the Battle of Ueno at the end of the shogunate, when the town burned; the Great Kantō Earthquake; the Pacific War; the 2011 Tōhoku disaster. 「数々の戦災や震災に見舞われても暖簾を守り続けることができたのは、伊豆榮を支えて下さる多くのお客様がいて下さったからこそ。」 The business incorporated as 株式会社伊豆榮 on 22 September 1950 and today runs three Tokyo restaurants — 本店 and 不忍亭 in Ueno, 梅川亭 in Ueno Park — with more than a hundred cooks; the Nagatachō branch closed on 31 January 2022. The ninth-generation okami, Yoshimi Doi, is also the company's president and signs its public statements. The craft claims are specific. The eel is Mikawa Isshiki, and within that a small branded line called 三河鰻咲 (Mikawa Mansaku), raised in conditions closer to wild than farmed. The method is strictly edomae: split from the back, skewered, charcoal-grilled, then steamed to drive off surplus fat, then dipped in tare and grilled again — a discipline the trade sums up as 「裂き三年、串八年、焼き一生」, three years to learn to split, eight to skewer, a lifetime to grill. And the tare is the boast: soy sauce and mirin, nothing else, rested two weeks to a month so the edges come off. The house makes a point of the consequence — because there is no sugar, the gloss on the eel dies within seconds of the lid coming off the box, so 「一瞬の美しさにもご注目ください」: look quickly.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「江戸前の鰻という世界に誇れる食文化を後世に伝え、一人でも多くのお客様にその美味しさを伝え続けることを使命に、これからも精進してまいります。」 — the house reads its own longevity as a debt to customers rather than an achievement.
chef_bio.specialty: うな重 松 ¥3,960 / 竹 ¥5,060 / 梅 ¥6,160 with soup and pickles; 蒲焼 ¥3,850–¥6,050; 白焼 ¥6,380; 御会席料理 松 ¥9,900 through 特 ¥22,000; a 鰻 course at ¥16,500 with liver skewer, shirayaki and uzaku; additive-free 鰻佃煮 in a gift box ¥2,484

anecdotes.text: The tare has no sugar in it — 「材料は醤油と味醂のみ」 — and is rested two weeks to a month before use. The visible consequence is that the shine on the eel vanishes almost immediately once the box is opened.
The house dates itself to the reign of Yoshimune, the eighth shogun, when Ikenohata was lined with 小屋掛け eel shacks and Izuei was one of them.
The ninth-generation okami, Yoshimi Doi, is also the company's representative director — the greeting on the corporate page is signed 「九代目女将　土肥好美」.
Parking was restricted from 1 July 2024 to guests who have booked a private room, with everyone else asked to come by public transport.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The company's own site supplies the Yoshimune-era origin at Ikenohata, the disaster list, the 「九代目女将 土肥好美」 signature, the corporate record (株式会社伊豆榮, 〒110-0005 上野2-12-22, incorporated 22 September 1950, president 土肥好美), the Mikawa Isshiki / 三河鰻咲 sourcing, the soy-and-mirin-only tare, the edomae grilling method, the complete price list, and a branch directory giving the honten's 11:00–21:00 hours, its year-round opening and the weekday 15:00–16:30 restriction to unajū and kabayaki only. Tabelog 13003586 independently confirms the address, the phone 03-3831-0954, 270 seats and the same hours. The company's news archive records the closure of the Nagatachō branch on 31 January 2022 and the July 2024 parking change.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One charcoal grill for both tare-glazed and plain eel, with the tare applied over the fire. A 270-seat banquet house with private rooms and a large brigade — assume no isolation of any single order.
Every kaiseki course on the published menu contains a 揚物 (deep-fried) course.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tare is 「醤油と味醂のみ」 — ordinary wheat soy sauce and mirin, no sugar and no tamari alternative. Everything labelled 重, 丼 or 蒲焼 is coated in it.

vegan_cross_contact.text: An eel house with a dashi-based kaiseki kitchen; the shop's own copy sells the 「出汁のやさしい香り」 of its Japanese courses. No animal-free preparation exists.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen statement anywhere on the Japanese site or its English version. Reservations are taken by telephone only, which at least means a dietary request would reach a person before you arrive.

positives.text: 白焼 — plain-grilled eel with no tare — is a standing menu item at ¥6,380, and the ¥16,500 鰻 kaiseki course includes it. It is the one dish here a wheat-avoidant diner could build on.
The tare contains no sugar, and the takeaway 鰻佃煮 is stated to use 「防腐剤・添加物は一切使用しておりません」 — a short, legible ingredient list by the standards of the genre.

cultural_comfort.note: A grand old restaurant that is nonetheless straightforward for a visitor: 270 seats over several floors at Ikenohata, open every day of the year except 31 December and 1 January, straight through 11:00 to 21:00, with an English version of the official site. Lunch is the easy entry — unajū at ¥3,960 with soup and pickles, no reservation needed. Courses and private rooms are telephone bookings, and a private room adds a 15% service charge. Two things to know: on weekdays between 15:00 and 16:30 the kitchen serves only unajū and kabayaki, and since July 2024 the car park is reserved for private-room bookings, so come by train — it is three minutes from Ueno-Hirokōji, Keisei-Ueno and Ueno-Okachimachi.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Tabelog nationwide search for 伊豆栄 returns five entries; this is 鰻割烹 伊豆栄 本店 (13003586) at 上野2-12-22, 177 m from Keisei-Ueno, matching the light record's 「京成上野・池之端」. Address and hours cross-checked against the company's own branch directory. CATEGORY FLAG: filed as MOM_AND_POP, but 株式会社伊豆榮 runs three Tokyo restaurants with over a hundred cooks and a 270-seat flagship — a family-owned company, not a mom-and-pop shop. DATE NOTE: Tabelog lists 「オープン日 1985年9月1日」, which is a building or listing date; the company itself dates the business to the Yoshimune era (1720s–30s) and its incorporation to 22 September 1950.

name: ぽん多本家
cuisine: The shop where the Japanese pork cutlet was invented, still run by the founder's family since 1905 — トンカツ's ancestor, カツレツ, cut from the lean heart of the loin and fried for ten minutes in the shop's own rendered lard, ¥2,700; also anago fry ¥3,780, prawn croquette ¥2,700, tongue stew ¥4,320, rice and red-miso soup ¥540
neighborhood: Ueno 3-chōme on the Okachimachi side of Ueno-Hirokōji — 143 m from Ueno-Hirokōji (Tokyo Metro Ginza line) and Ueno-Okachimachi (Toei Ōedo line), about 3 min from JR Okachimachi's south exit (Yamanote / Keihin-Tōhoku)
gf_detail: No, and it is the wheat that makes the dish. The カツレツ is built by dredging the loin in flour, then egg, then coarse breadcrumbs — 「小麦粉、卵、粗めのパン粉の順に衣をつけ」 — and lowered into lard at 120–130°C to finish above 160°C over more than ten minutes. The tongue stew is a demi-glace, which is a flour roux. The croquettes are breaded. There is no unbreaded dish on the published menu, the shop has no website and publishes no allergen information, and it is a 33-seat house with a queue. One genuinely unusual fact, useful to somebody with a seed-oil or soy problem rather than a celiac: the frying medium is not vegetable oil but lard the shop renders itself from the fat trimmed off its own loins.
vegan_detail: No. A Meiji-era 洋食 house whose entire menu is pork, beef tongue, prawn and conger eel, fried in animal fat. The only non-animal items on the list are rice and pickles, and even the miso soup is a red-miso stock. Nothing here is prepared away from meat.

chef_bio.chef_name: 島田良彦 (Yoshihiko Shimada), 四代目
roles: 四代目店主 (fourth-generation owner-chef)
founder: 島田信二郎 (Shinjirō Shimada), formerly of the 宮内省大膳寮 (Imperial Household Ministry's Board of the Imperial Kitchen)
chef_bio.origin: Ueno, Taitō-ku — the shop has been on this corner since 1905
chef_bio.background: Ponta Honke is where a great deal of modern Japanese home cooking comes from, and it started with a court chef going into business for himself. 島田信二郎 cooked Western food at the 宮内省大膳寮, the Imperial Household Ministry's kitchen bureau, and in 1905 (明治38年) opened his own place in Ueno with a single organising idea: 「ご飯に合う洋食」, Western food that goes with rice. What he made to that brief was カツレツ — a veal-style cutlet reworked in pork, fried rather than pan-sautéed, cut into chopstick-sized pieces and served with rice — and that dish is the direct ancestor of tonkatsu as the whole country now eats it. The shop is on its fourth generation. 島田良彦 trained three years at the Hilltop Hotel (山の上ホテル) before joining the family kitchen at twenty-one, and took over at thirty-six when his father died; a fifth generation is reported to be working the stoves alongside him. The method has not been simplified with time. Only the lean centre of the loin is used and all the fat is trimmed away — then that same fat is rendered down into lard, and the lard is what the cutlet is fried in, 100% house-made. The cutlet goes in at 120–130°C and comes out above 160–190°C after more than ten minutes, because, as Shimada puts it, 「赤身と脂身の部分ではそれぞれ最適な揚げ時間が異なる」 — lean and fat want different frying times, so you cannot simply drop it in hot oil. It is halved horizontally first, then cut down into pieces. His statement of the trade is three items long: 「材料を吟味すること、二つ目は上手に揚げ油を取ること、そして三つ目は技術を高めること」 — scrutinise the ingredients, render your frying fat properly, and keep improving the technique. Thirty-three seats over three floors — a three-seat counter downstairs, tables on the first floor, a nine-seat tatami room above. Closed Mondays. The shop keeps no website; the queue does the marketing, and Tabelog rates it 3.77 and lists it among the 洋食 EAST 百名店 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「材料を吟味すること、二つ目は上手に揚げ油を取ること、そして三つ目は技術を高めること」 — and the founder's brief, unchanged for 120 years: Western cooking that belongs beside a bowl of rice.
chef_bio.specialty: カツレツ ¥2,700 — the original, fried in house-rendered lard; アナゴフライ ¥3,780; 車海老のクリームコロッケ ¥2,700; タンシチュー ¥4,320; ご飯・赤だし・お新香 ¥540

anecdotes.text: The fat trimmed off the loin is not discarded — it is rendered into the lard the cutlet is then fried in, so the dish cooks in its own by-product.
The frying takes over ten minutes, starting at 120–130°C and finishing at 160–190°C, because 「赤身と脂身の部分ではそれぞれ最適な揚げ時間が異なる」.
The fourth generation spent three years at the Hilltop Hotel before entering the family kitchen at twenty-one, and inherited the shop at thirty-six on his father's death.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Gnavi's dressing feature is the fullest source: it gives the founder 島田信二郎 and his post at the 宮内省大膳寮, the 1905 founding, the 「ご飯に合う洋食」 concept, the fourth generation 島田良彦 with his Hilltop Hotel apprenticeship and his age at succession, the complete frying method (lean-only loin, house-rendered lard, 120–130°C to 160–190°C over ten-plus minutes, flour-egg-panko breading), the cutting method and the current prices. Tabelog 13003587 independently confirms the address 上野3-23-3, phone 03-3831-2351, the 1905 (明治38年) founding, 33 seats over three floors, the Monday closure, the current service times and the 洋食 EAST 百名店 2025 selection. Several Japanese food and history sites corroborate the imperial-chef origin, though they split between the spellings 信二郎 and 信治郎 for the founder's given name.

gf_cross_contamination.text: There is no unbreaded item on the menu. Flour, egg and panko are the whole technique, and the lard is shared by the cutlets, the croquettes and the conger fry.
Thirty-three seats over three floors with a queue and no published allergy process; the shop has no website of any kind.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Beyond the breading, the tongue stew is a flour-thickened demi-glace and the accompaniments are the usual 洋食 sauces. No tamari, no wheat-free preparation.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The frying medium itself is pork lard rendered in house, so even the vegetable garnish and the croquettes are cooked in animal fat.

staff_allergy_handling.text: None published anywhere. No website, no English page, no allergen notice on Tabelog.

positives.text: The frying fat is 100% lard the shop renders from its own loin trimmings rather than a blended vegetable oil — relevant to a soy or seed-oil avoidance, though not to gluten.

cultural_comfort.note: Small, revered and entirely Japanese-facing: 33 seats over three floors behind a heavy old door on Ueno 3-chōme, no website, no English menu found anywhere, and a queue at both services. Closed Mondays; lunch 11:00–14:00 (last order 13:45), dinner from 16:30 (16:00 on Sundays and holidays) to 20:20. Expect ¥4,000–¥5,999 a head. The dish is easy to order by name — 「カツレツ」 — and hard to discuss; if you need to explain a dietary restriction, this is not the room for it.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Tabelog nationwide search for ぽん多本家 returns exactly one shop, 13003587, at 上野3-23-3, 143 m from Ueno-Hirokōji — matching the light record. GF and vegan both left at no, which the light sweep already had right. NAME-SPELLING NOTE for the reviewer: Japanese sources split between 島田信二郎 and 島田信治郎 for the founder; this record uses 信二郎, the spelling used by gnavi's dressing feature and by most literary sources.

name: 油そば専門店 浜そば 本店
cuisine: A five-seat abura-soba counter thirty seconds from Yushima station, open since 2008 — brothless wheat noodles tossed in a soy tare simmered from domestic chicken and pork and a purpose-blended oil, ¥650 regular, ¥750 large, ¥850 double, with toppings from ¥50
neighborhood: Yushima 3-chōme on the Ueno side of Bunkyō-ku — 152 m (about 30 seconds) from exit 2 of Yushima Station on the Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line, and about 5 min from JR Okachimachi
hours_raw: [月～土] 11:30～23:30　[日・祝] 11:30～21:30　定休日：不定休　※麺がなくなり次第終了（食べログは月～土 11:30～22:00、日・祝 11:30～17:00 と記載 — 公式サイトの方が新しい）
gf_detail: No, on both counts at once. 油そば is a wheat-noodle dish by definition — Chinese-style alkaline noodles, no broth, tossed in a sauce at the bottom of the bowl — so the noodle itself is wheat. And the sauce is 「秘伝醤油ダレ」, a soy-sauce tare, which is also wheat. There is nothing else on the menu; the shop sells one dish in two variants plus toppings. The takeaway packs are the same noodles and the same tare. No allergen information is published.
vegan_detail: No. The tare is made by simmering domestic chicken and pork for hours to draw out the extract, then combining it with the house soy sauce — 「国産の鳥、豚などの具材を長時間煮込みエキスを抽出し、独自製法で作られた秘伝の醤油ダレとかけ合わせ」 — so the base of the only dish is meat stock. The standard bowl is finished with teriyaki chicken and menma, and 温玉 (soft egg) is a topping. There is no meat-free version.

roles: 株式会社Triple Axel (operating company)
chef_bio.origin: Yushima, Bunkyō-ku — the shop opened here on 17 November 2008
chef_bio.background: Hamasoba is a one-dish shop with five counter seats, thirty seconds from exit 2 at Yushima, and it has been selling the same bowl since 17 November 2008 under the line 「変わらぬ味を守り続けています」. Abura-soba is Tokyo's brothless noodle: a tare sits at the bottom of the bowl, the noodles go in hot, and you toss them yourself. The shop's two stated obsessions are the tare and the oil. The tare is a soy sauce base combined with an extract simmered for hours from domestic chicken and pork — 「上質なコクと深みがある秘伝醤油ダレ」. The oil is the more unusual claim, and the shop makes a health argument for it at some length: independently developed, rich in DHA, EPA and the alpha-linolenic acid found in perilla, and — in the shop's own telling — capable of lowering LDL and total cholesterol, raising HDL, reducing triglycerides, and helping against cancer, arteriosclerosis, hypertension and dementia, as well as being good for dieting, for the skin and for easing allergy symptoms. That is a nutraceutical claim of a scale no small noodle counter can substantiate and it should be read as marketing, not evidence; it is quoted here because the shop puts it at the centre of its identity — 「ただ美味しいというものだけではなく、他社さんとの差別化を図り体も一緒に健康になるというコンセプト」. A bowl is ¥650 (¥750 large, ¥850 double); extra pork is ¥300, everything else ¥50–¥100. Takeaway tare-and-noodle packs run ¥900 for two servings to ¥2,600 for six, and the shop delivers around Ueno and Yushima on orders over ¥2,000. Tabelog rates it 3.51 across more than four hundred reviews. No individual chef is named anywhere.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「変わらぬ味を守り続けています」 — one bowl, unchanged, made faster than you can sit down.
chef_bio.specialty: 浜そば 並 ¥650 / 大 ¥750 / W盛 ¥850; 辛味浜そば at the same prices; 肉増し ¥300, 全部増し ¥350, メンマ・温玉・ネギごま・キムチ・ザーサイ ¥100 each, 辛味もやし ¥50; お土産セット 2食 ¥900 / 4食 ¥1,800 / 6食 ¥2,600

anecdotes.text: Five counter seats and nothing else — the shop's own selling point is speed, thirty seconds from Yushima exit 2, and it closes when the noodles run out.

The shop's health claim for its bespoke oil is extraordinary in scope: DHA, EPA and alpha-linolenic acid, said to lower LDL and total cholesterol, raise HDL, cut triglycerides and help against cancer, arteriosclerosis, hypertension and dementia — as well as aiding dieting, skin and allergy symptoms. Nothing supports it beyond the shop's own copy.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The shop's own site carries the tare and oil copy, the complete price list, the takeaway and delivery terms, the address 〒113-0034 東京都文京区湯島3-46-2, the phone 03-3831-0641, the current hours ([月～土] 11:30～23:30, [日・祝] 11:30～21:30, 不定休) and the operating company 株式会社Triple Axel. Tabelog 13058424 independently confirms the address and phone, gives the 17 November 2008 opening, five counter seats, the under-¥999 price band, the 30-seconds-from-exit-2 walk and the sell-out closing, and lists slightly earlier hours than the shop's own site (月～土 11:30–22:00, 日・祝 11:30–17:00), which is why hours_status here is irregular.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One pot of boiling water for wheat noodles and nothing else on the menu. There is no non-wheat item to protect.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The single sauce is a 「秘伝醤油ダレ」 — a soy-sauce tare. No tamari version is offered and no allergen list is published.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The tare itself is built on chicken and pork simmered for hours: 「国産の鳥、豚などの具材を長時間煮込みエキスを抽出し」. Even a bowl ordered without toppings is meat-based.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Nothing published. The shop's health page discusses allergy symptoms in the abstract as a benefit of its oil, which is not the same thing as an allergen protocol and should not be mistaken for one.

cultural_comfort.note: A five-seat counter thirty seconds from Yushima station exit 2, selling one bowl at ¥650 and turning it around fast. No English menu, no reservations, and no room to linger — but also nothing to decide beyond size and toppings, which makes it one of the easier Japanese counters to use with no Japanese at all. Open 11:30 to 23:30 Monday to Saturday and to 21:30 on Sundays and holidays per the shop's own site, closing earlier when the noodles run out; closing days are irregular. Takeaway and local delivery are available.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Tabelog nationwide search for 浜そば returns twelve shops, mostly Kanagawa station-platform soba stands; the abura-soba specialist in the light record is 13058424 at 文京区湯島3-46-2, 152 m from Yushima — matching. CATEGORY FLAG: filed as MOM_AND_POP; the operator is 株式会社Triple Axel. GF and vegan left at no. FOR A HUMAN: the shop's own site makes unsubstantiated medical claims for its cooking oil (cancer, arteriosclerosis, hypertension, dementia prevention). Nothing of that is repeated as fact in this record, and it should not be surfaced in the app.

name: 和楽庵
address_ja: 〒110-0016 東京都台東区台東4-32-7 第2宮地ビル1F
cuisine: A Honjinbō-group soba house behind Okachimachi's north exit — buckwheat milled on a stone quern each morning and cut by hand, sold as a 三色もり of yuzu, seiro and coarse inaka (¥1,300), alongside Toyosu sashimi and Iwate duck; ¥1,000–¥1,999 at lunch, ¥6,000–¥7,999 at night with a 10% service charge after 17:00
neighborhood: Taitō 4-chōme behind Okachimachi station — 2 min from JR Okachimachi's north exit (Yamanote / Keihin-Tōhoku), 1 min from exit 3 of Ueno-Okachimachi (Toei Ōedo line), 68 m from Naka-Okachimachi (Tokyo Metro Hibiya line)
hours_raw: 月曜日～金曜日 11:30～15:00（L.O.14:30）、17:00～22:00（L.O.21:00）／土曜日・日曜日・祝日 11:30～21:00（通し営業、L.O.20:00）　定休日：無休（本陣房グループ公式サイト）※食べログは「定休日 日曜日」と記載 — 日曜に行く場合は 03-5688-1345 で要確認。17:00よりサービス料10%
gf_detail: No. The group publishes its own soba list and it is wheat from end to end: the tsuyu is standard wheat soy sauce, the tempura sits on half the menu (穴子天, 海老天, 野菜天, よくばり天), and the 三色もり that is the house signature includes a ゆず切り, a flavoured noodle that needs a binder to hold the citrus. Nothing in the group's published material claims a jūwari or wheat-free noodle — the boast is 「石臼挽き手打ちそば」, stone-milled and hand-cut, which says nothing about the ratio. There is no allergen page for the group and no gluten-free item anywhere across its fifteen restaurants.
vegan_detail: Nothing published, and the odds are poor. The group's soba tsuyu is a bonito dashi, the 野菜天もり (¥1,500) is a vegetable tempura but in an egg-and-wheat batter, and the shop's own selling point is that the owner buys fish at Toyosu every morning and grills Iwate duck. The one plausible plant-based order — vegetable tempura eaten with salt instead of tsuyu — has not been confirmed as available and the batter has not been ruled out. Ask, in Japanese, before you go.

roles: one of about fifteen restaurants in the 日本橋 本陣房 group (本陣房, 味喜庵, 吉仙, 和楽庵, 五大, 天祥庵, 魚富, 魚祥, 遊友魚港)
the group also runs 御徒町 和楽庵 はなれ one street away
chef_bio.origin: Okachimachi, Taitō-ku — this branch opened on 22 February 2014
chef_bio.background: Warakuan is the Okachimachi arm of Honjinbō, a Tokyo soba group that has quietly grown to about fifteen restaurants clustered around Nihonbashi, Shimbashi, Kanda and Ueno, most of them soba houses and several of them fish izakaya. The group's proposition is consistent across all of them and stated on the group site as 「石臼挽き手打ちそば」: buckwheat stone-milled in house and cut by hand each day, sold in three characters — a plain せいろ, a coarse 田舎 cut thick, and a ゆず切り with citrus worked into the dough — and offered together as the 三色もり, which is the group's signature at ¥1,300. Around the soba the shops build a full izakaya: 江戸前 conger and prawn tempura, 京都聖護院 herring in hot soba, duck seiro, and a fish list. What makes the Okachimachi branch its own place rather than a clone is the sourcing and the room. The proprietor goes to Toyosu himself each morning and buys the fish, which is why the sashimi assortment (five or six kinds) is the thing people order alongside the noodles, and the interior is built as a set of 完全個室 in white wood and earthen wall, sized from two to twelve people — a business-entertaining room as much as a soba shop. It opened on 22 February 2014, seats 32, and stands two minutes behind Okachimachi's north exit; the group opened a second room, 和楽庵 はなれ, on the next street in 2017. A 10% service charge applies from 17:00 across the group. No individual chef is named in any published source.
chef_bio.philosophy: Mill it that morning, cut it by hand, and let the owner's own Toyosu buying carry the rest of the menu.
chef_bio.specialty: 三色もり (ゆず・せいろ・田舎) ¥1,300 and 三色大もり ¥1,600; 石臼自家製粉 せいろもり ¥700; 粗挽き太打ちそば 田舎もり ¥800; 鴨せいろ ¥1,800; 穴子天もり / 海老天もり ¥1,800; よくばり天もり ¥2,500; sashimi assortment; 個室 for 2–12

anecdotes.text: The group's noodle is sold as three characters at once — 「名物 三色もり ゆず・せいろ・田舎」 — a citrus-cut, a plain seiro and a coarse country cut on the same tray for ¥1,300.
The proprietor buys the fish himself at Toyosu each morning, which is why a soba house's most-ordered dish alongside the noodles is a five-or-six-kind sashimi plate.
A 10% service charge applies from 17:00 across every Honjinbō-group restaurant, and prices differ slightly branch to branch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The Honjinbō group's own site lists 御徒町 和楽庵 at 〒110-0016 東京都台東区台東4-32-7 第2宮地ビル1階, phone 03-5688-1345, with hours 月～金 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:00, 土日祝 11:30–21:00, and 定休日 無休, plus the walking directions from Okachimachi north exit and Ueno-Okachimachi exit 3; its soba page gives the complete noodle list with prices and the 17:00 service charge. Tabelog 13166630 independently confirms the address, the alternate phone, 32 seats, the 22 February 2014 opening, the ¥1,000–¥1,999 lunch and ¥6,000–¥7,999 dinner bands, the stone-milling and hand-cutting, the Toyosu sourcing and the private rooms — but records 定休日 日曜日, which contradicts the group site's 無休. The group site also confirms that 和楽庵 はなれ, one street away at 台東4-31-6, is a separate restaurant with its own Sunday closure.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 32-seat soba kitchen cutting noodles on a dusted board and frying tempura across half its menu — 穴子天, 海老天, 野菜天, よくばり天 in both hot and cold versions.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard wheat soy sauce in the tsuyu; no tamari is offered anywhere across the fifteen-restaurant group, and no allergen page exists on the group site.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi in the tsuyu, an owner who buys fish at Toyosu daily, duck and herring on the noodle list. Nothing is prepared away from animal ingredients.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen statement on the group site or on Tabelog. The private rooms and the reservation line do at least mean a request can be made in advance by telephone.

positives.text: 完全個室 for two to twelve people, which makes a quiet dietary conversation possible in a way a counter does not.

cultural_comfort.note: A comfortable, mid-priced group restaurant rather than an intimidating specialist — 32 seats and a set of private rooms two minutes behind Okachimachi's north exit, open through the afternoon at weekends, cards accepted, and a menu of recognisable soba with prices printed on the group's website. Everything is in Japanese and no English menu was found. Note two traps: a 10% service charge is added from 17:00, and the sources disagree about Sundays — the group's own site says 無休 (never closed) while Tabelog says closed Sundays. Ring 03-5688-1345 before a Sunday visit. Do not confuse it with 和楽庵 はなれ, a separate room one street away at 台東4-31-6.

Tabelog nationwide search for 和楽庵 returns eleven shops across Japan; the Tokyo one is 13166630 at 台東4-32-7 第2宮地ビル1F, 68 m from 仲御徒町 — which is what the light record's 「Nakametacho Station」 was a garbling of (仲御徒町 = Naka-okachimachi). GF downgraded ask → no.
