neighborhood: Ueno 6-chōme, basement of the Ueno Six Road building — 97 m from Naka-Okachimachi (Tokyo Metro Hibiya line), 1 min from JR Okachimachi (Yamanote / Keihin-Tōhoku), 5 min from JR Ueno
gf_detail: No. The shop's own copy describes 「厳選した国内産の玄蕎麦を、特製注文の石臼で丁寧にその日の分のみ挽いております」 — domestic buckwheat, milled fresh daily on a custom stone quern — but never claims a jūwari or wheat-free noodle, and its three cuts include a ゆず切り, a flavoured noodle that needs a binder. Its best-sellers are the 三色もり and 海老天ぷら蕎麦 (¥1,300, two prawns), so a tempura pan runs all service; the banquet courses are built on 自家製さつま揚げ (fish cakes, which are usually starch- and often wheat-bound), 出汁巻玉子 and seasonal tempura. The tsuyu is wheat soy sauce. No allergen information is published.
vegan_detail: Nothing published, and the shape of the menu is against it. The tsuyu is a dashi the shop advertises for its aroma; the owner shops at Tsukiji each morning and the sashimi plate is a headline item; the courses are fish cakes, rolled omelette and grilled free-range chicken. A vegan would be down to plain soba eaten dry and would have to establish the dashi and the tempura batter first. Ask in Japanese; there is no vegetarian claim anywhere.

roles: owner-proprietor (unnamed in all sources) — buys the fish at Tsukiji himself each morning
the shop is widely described by Japanese reviewers as 本陣房系列 — founded by alumni of the 日本橋 本陣房 soba group, though it does not appear on that group's own restaurant list
chef_bio.origin: Okachimachi, Taitō-ku — the shop opened in 2008 in the basement of the Ueno Six Road building
chef_bio.background: Shinsen-an sits a floor below street level a minute from Okachimachi station, and it is a soba shop the way a good izakaya is a soba shop: the noodles are the reason it exists and the sake list is why people stay. It opened in 2008 and Japanese reviewers place it in the Honjinbō lineage — 「本陣房系列の蕎麦屋が上野にできたと聞いて訪れた心洗庵」 — the Nihonbashi/Shimbashi soba group whose alumni have seeded several Okachimachi shops; note that the group's own current restaurant list does not include it, so it is best described as a spin-off rather than a branch. The soba is made the group way and better documented than most: 「厳選した国内産の玄蕎麦を、特製注文の石臼で丁寧にその日の分のみ挽いております」 — selected domestic whole buckwheat, milled on a stone quern built to order, only as much as the day needs — and the shop makes a point of the water: 「職人が一滴の水加減にもこだわり最高の状態を見極め」, judging the dough a drop at a time, cut fresh every morning. Three characters are offered, a yuzu-scented cut, an Edo-style blend and a coarse thick country cut, sold together as the ¥1,350 三色もり, which is the shop's best-seller. The fish is the owner's own doing: he goes to Tsukiji every morning, and the shop says the routes he has built there over many years are why a five-or-six-kind sashimi plate can be ¥3,600 for two. The sake is the third leg — thirty to forty labels from across Japan, rotated with seasonal limited releases, with an unusually deep 十四代 list from junmai ginjō up to daiginjō including bottles the shop describes as hard to get. Twenty-eight seats on a single sofa-seated floor, private hire from 25 to 36 people, free wifi, children welcome, closed Sundays.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「挽きたて 打ちたて 茹でたて」 — milled, cut and boiled on the same morning; the shop treats the interval between those three as the whole argument.
chef_bio.specialty: 三色もり ¥1,350 (best-seller); 海老天ぷら蕎麦 ¥1,300 with two prawns; 刺身盛り合わせ ¥3,600 for two, five or six kinds from Tsukiji; 手打ち蕎麦と鴨鍋コース ¥7,980 with two and a half hours of drinks; a 十四代-led list of 30–40 regional sakes

anecdotes.text: The stone quern is not a generic mill but 「特製注文の石臼」, made to the shop's order, and it grinds only the day's quantity.
The owner's Tsukiji routes are the shop's stated reason for cheap sashimi: 「長年足を運ぶことで、オーナーが築き上げた独自のルートで新鮮な魚を安価で入荷しております」.
The sake list leads with Jūyondai from junmai ginjō to daiginjō, including bottles the shop says are hard to obtain even within the brand.

Japanese reviewers consistently file it with the Honjinbō family of Okachimachi soba shops alongside 吉仙 and 上野 味喜庵, one of them noting that some of these were started by group alumni who have since gone independent.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The shop's own gnavi-hosted official page (soba-ueno-shinsenan.gorp.jp) supplies the stone-milling and daily-cutting copy, the Tsukiji sourcing, the sake programme, the current hours and Sunday closure, 28 seats, private hire for 25–36, the card list, the free wifi and the children-welcome flag, plus the best-seller prices (三色もり ¥1,350, 海老天ぷら蕎麦 ¥1,300, 刺身盛り合わせ ¥3,600). Tabelog 13057433 independently confirms the address 上野6-1-6 上野シックスロードB1, the phones, 28 seats, the 2008 opening, the price bands and the three soba characters. Multiple independent Japanese reviewers (Tabelog, Retty, umai-net, a personal blog) identify it as a Honjinbō-lineage shop; the Honjinbō group's own restaurant directory lists fifteen shops and does not include it, which is why this record calls it a spin-off rather than a branch.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A 28-seat basement kitchen milling and cutting soba on site every morning, with a tempura pan running for the ¥1,300 prawn tempura soba and the seasonal course tempura.
The banquet courses lead with 自家製さつま揚げ — house-made fried fish cakes, which are normally bound with starch and frequently with wheat flour.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Ordinary wheat soy sauce in the tsuyu; no tamari, and no wheat-free noodle claim anywhere in the shop's material.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Dashi tsuyu, daily Tsukiji fish, rolled egg and grilled chicken through the course menus. There is no animal-free preparation.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen statement on the shop's own page or on Tabelog.

positives.text: Children are welcome, free wifi, and the room can be taken over privately for 25–36 people — a low-pressure setting to make a request in, if you can make it in Japanese.

cultural_comfort.note: A relaxed basement room a minute from Okachimachi station, 28 seats on one sofa-seated floor with a clear view across it, cards accepted, free wifi, children welcome, and a soba lunch at ¥1,000–¥1,999 that needs no reservation. Everything is in Japanese — the shop's page, the sake list, the seasonal specials — and no English menu was found anywhere. Closed Sundays. Evenings are drinking-course territory at ¥5,500–¥7,980 a head and worth booking; it is the sort of place where the sake list, not the noodle, decides how the night goes.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Tabelog nationwide search for 心洗庵 returns exactly one restaurant, 13057433, at 上野6-1-6 上野シックスロードB1, 97 m from 仲御徒町 — close to the light record's 「Okachimachi Station」. LINEAGE NOTE for the reviewer: Japanese reviewers uniformly call this a 本陣房系列 shop, but the Honjinbō group's own directory of fifteen restaurants does not list it, so this record describes it as a spin-off founded by group alumni rather than a group branch — do not merge it with 和楽庵 (tokyo3__231), which is a group restaurant. GF downgraded ask → no.

name: 伊豆栄 不忍亭
cuisine: The quieter, more grown-up room of the 300-year-old Izuei eel house, two hundred metres from the flagship — the same Mikawa Isshiki eel and the same sugarless soy-and-mirin tare, 122 seats of private-room dining, unajū ¥3,960–¥6,160, shirayaki ¥6,380, kaiseki to ¥22,000; also the branch that runs Izuei's delivery service
neighborhood: Ueno 2-chōme, just south of the flagship on the Shinobazu Pond side — 3 min from Ueno-Hirokōji (Tokyo Metro Ginza line), 3 min from Yushima (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line), 5 min from JR Ueno
gf_detail: Same kitchen discipline as the flagship, same single opening. Izuei's tare is 「醤油と味醂のみ」 — soy sauce and mirin, no sugar — and Japanese soy sauce is a wheat ferment, so every 重, 丼 and 蒲焼 is wheat. The one item worth a conversation is 白焼 at ¥6,380, plain-grilled eel with no tare, eaten with wasabi and salt; bring your own tamari and it becomes a possible meal with rice and pickles. But it comes off the same charcoal as the tare-basted eels, all the kaiseki courses include a 揚物, and 122 seats of private rooms means a large brigade. Nothing is published about allergens on the Japanese site or its English version. Reservations are by telephone, so the request can at least be made in advance.
vegan_detail: No. An eel restaurant with a dashi-based kaiseki kitchen; the courses run 先付・前菜・椀物・お造り・煮物・酢の物 and finish with unajū, and the company's own copy sells the dashi aroma of its Japanese cooking. There is no vegetarian course and no published capability for one.

chef_bio.chef_name: 土肥好美 (Yoshimi Doi), 九代目女将
roles: 九代目女将 / ninth-generation okami and 代表取締役社長 of 株式会社伊豆榮
本店調理長 — a head chef of more than forty years overseeing 100+ cooks across the company's Tokyo restaurants
chef_bio.origin: Ueno, Taitō-ku — Shinobazu-tei opened on 1 March 2009, two hundred metres from the family's founding site at Ikenohata
chef_bio.background: Shinobazu-tei is the second of Izuei's three surviving Tokyo restaurants and the one the company describes as 「落ち着いた大人の空間」 — the calm, adult room, as against the 270-seat bustle of the honten two hundred metres north and the garden views of 梅川亭 up in Ueno Park. It opened on 1 March 2009 and seats 122, largely in private rooms. Everything material about the food is the house's, unchanged since the eighth shogun's reign: eel from Mikawa Isshiki under the 三河鰻咲 label, raised in conditions closer to wild than farmed; the edomae method of splitting from the back, skewering, charcoal-grilling, steaming off the surplus fat and grilling again in tare; and the tare itself, made from soy sauce and mirin only and rested two weeks to a month, with no sugar at all — which is why the gloss dies within seconds of the lid coming off the box. The house's own words for the craft are 「裂き三年、串八年、焼き一生」. Shinobazu-tei carries one duty the others do not: it runs Izuei's 出前, the delivery arm, and when the Nagatachō branch closed on 31 January 2022 it was Shinobazu-tei that took over that business and the enquiry line. The company signs its public notices 「九代目女将　土肥好美」, and its non-eel side is a traditional kaiseki kitchen under a head chef of forty years' standing, with more than a hundred cooks across the group. Closed Wednesdays, and the hours can shift when a sightseeing-bus booking is in.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「江戸前の鰻という世界に誇れる食文化を後世に伝え、一人でも多くのお客様にその美味しさを伝え続けることを使命に」 — the same house creed as the flagship, delivered in a quieter room.
chef_bio.specialty: うな重 松 ¥3,960 / 竹 ¥5,060 / 梅 ¥6,160; 蒲焼 ¥3,850–¥6,050; 白焼 ¥6,380; 御会席料理 松 ¥9,900 to 特 ¥22,000, and a 鰻 course at ¥16,500 with liver skewer, shirayaki and uzaku; delivery of unajū and bentō for meetings, memorials and celebrations

anecdotes.text: When Izuei's Nagatachō branch closed on 31 January 2022, Shinobazu-tei absorbed its delivery business and its enquiry line: 「出前等のお問い合わせ、ご用命は、不忍亭が業務を引き継いでおります。」
The company positions this branch by mood rather than menu — 「落ち着いた大人の空間」, against the flagship's 「伊豆榮始まりの地」 and 梅川亭's 「閑雅な眺望」.
The tare has no sugar in it, which the house treats as a feature with a consequence: the shine on the eel is gone in a moment, so 「一瞬の美しさにもご注目ください」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The company's own branch directory gives 伊豆栄 不忍亭 at 〒110-0005 東京都台東区上野2-11-19, phone 03-3832-0785, hours 11:00–14:30 and 17:00–21:00 with an extended weekend/holiday lunch to 15:00, 定休日 水曜日, the sightseeing-bus caveat, the delivery service and the station walking times. Its 伊豆榮とは, こだわり and お品書き pages supply the Yoshimune-era origin, the 「九代目女将 土肥好美」 signature, the corporate record, the Mikawa Isshiki / 三河鰻咲 sourcing, the soy-and-mirin-only tare and the shared price list. A 2022 notice records the Nagatachō closure and the transfer of its delivery business here. Tabelog 13019022 independently confirms the address, phone, 122 seats, the 1 March 2009 opening, the Wednesday closure and the ¥6,000–¥7,999 lunch / ¥10,000–¥14,999 dinner bands.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One charcoal grill for tare-glazed and plain eel alike, with the tare brushed on over the fire; a 122-seat private-room house with a large brigade.
Every kaiseki course on the published menu contains a 揚物 (deep-fried) course.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tare is 「醤油と味醂のみ」 — wheat soy sauce and mirin, with no tamari alternative offered. Every 重, 丼 and 蒲焼 is coated in it.

vegan_cross_contact.text: An eel house with a dashi kaiseki kitchen. No animal-free preparation exists on the premises.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergen statement on the Japanese site or its English version. Reservations are telephone-only, so a dietary request would at least reach a person before service.

positives.text: 白焼 — plain-grilled eel with no tare — is on the standing menu at ¥6,380, the one dish here a wheat-avoidant diner could build on.
Private rooms and telephone reservations make a dietary conversation practical in a way a counter would not, and the company's takeaway 佃煮 is stated to contain 「防腐剤・添加物は一切使用しておりません」.

cultural_comfort.note: The calm alternative to Izuei's flagship, two hundred metres away: 122 seats, mostly private rooms, three minutes from Ueno-Hirokōji and from Yushima, with an English version of the company site to read before you go. Lunch runs 11:00 to 14:30 on weekdays and to 15:00 at weekends and holidays; dinner 17:00 to 21:00; closed Wednesdays. Prices sit higher than the flagship's — Tabelog puts lunch at ¥6,000–¥7,999 and dinner at ¥10,000–¥14,999 — because this is where the course menus and the rooms are. Book by phone (03-3832-0785); note that a private room adds 15% service, and that hours can move when a sightseeing-bus reservation is in. This is also the branch that delivers.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED. Tabelog nationwide search for 伊豆栄 returns five entries; this is 鰻割烹 伊豆栄 不忍亭 (13019022) at 上野2-11-19, 258 m from 上野広小路 — matching the light record's 「台東区上野 (Ueno-Hirokoji Station)」. Address, hours and the Wednesday closure cross-checked against the company's own branch directory. This is a sibling of tokyo3__216 (伊豆栄 本店), two hundred metres away and a separate restaurant — keep both. CATEGORY FLAG: filed as MOM_AND_POP, but it is one of three Tokyo restaurants of 株式会社伊豆榮. The light record's 「江戸時代創業」 is correct: the house dates to the reign of the eighth shogun Yoshimune, though this particular room opened on 1 March 2009.

name: 浅草ときわ食堂
cuisine: A 1922 shokudō two doors from Kaminarimon, fourth generation, open from half past eight in the morning — grilled and simmered fish, tonkatsu, a famous wild-horse-mackerel fry and a daily board, mostly ¥880–¥1,880 with rice from ¥330 and four kinds of soup; 36 seats, and the cheapest honest meal on Tokyo's most expensive tourist street
neighborhood: Asakusa 1-chōme, two doors from Sensō-ji's Kaminarimon on Kaminarimon-dōri — 152 m from Asakusa Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza line, Toei Asakusa line, Tobu Skytree line)
hours_raw: 平日・土曜日 9:30～22:00／日・祝日 8:30～22:00（ラストオーダー 21:30）　休業日：水曜日（不定期）　※食べログは平日9:00開店・定休日水曜と記載。開店時刻は店の献立表に従う。
gf_detail: Genuinely worth asking here, which is rare in this shard. The shop prints an invitation on its own menu: 「食材でアレルギーがある方は御遠慮なく（お申し出）して下さい」 — if you have a food allergy, please say so without hesitation. And unlike a soba or eel house, a shokudō has plates that were never near flour: 刺身盛合 ¥1,680, まぐろ刺身 ¥1,080, にしん塩焼 ¥1,500 and さば塩焼 ¥880 are salt-grilled or raw, and rice (¥330) and お新香 (¥430) come plain. What still needs settling, dish by dish, is the soy sauce that will arrive with the sashimi (wheat — bring tamari), the miso in the soups (合わせ味噌 and 赤味噌 may be barley-containing 麦味噌 — ask), the 照りダレ on the silver cod and the 特製ダレ on the tofu steak, and the fryer, which runs continuously for tonkatsu, the aji fry, ham cutlets and karaage. Nothing is certified and nothing is separated; but there is a real conversation to have, and staff who invite it.
vegan_detail: Limited but real, by the standards of a 1922 teishoku shop. From the printed menu a vegan can assemble rice (¥330 small, ¥380 large), お新香 pickles (¥430), 納豆・梅干・やきのり at ¥100 each, ほうれん草おひたし ¥350, ほうれん草ごま和え ¥400 and 辛味噌きゅうり ¥480 — a plain, cheap, decent plate. Two things to confirm first, because both are usually dashi in a shop like this: the おひたし dressing and the miso soup. 茄子味噌 (¥880) is described as a sweet blended miso and may or may not carry dashi or pork. Everything else on the list is fish, egg or pork. The shop's open invitation to declare allergies is the way in.

chef_bio.chef_name: 牧信真 (Nobushige Maki), 四代目
roles: 四代目店主・社長 (fourth-generation owner and president)
株式会社ときわ
chef_bio.origin: Founded in 1922 in Honjo Koume Narihira-chō, near where the Skytree now stands; the family has been at Asakusa 1-3-3 for generations since
chef_bio.background: The shop's own menu carries its genealogy, printed as a family tree. It begins: 「当店は、大正一一年（一九二二年）に本所小梅業平町（スカイツリー近辺）にて、ときわ食堂総本店の第五支店として営業を始めました」 — it opened in 1922 as the fifth branch of the Tokiwa Shokudō main house, whose own root was the Meiji-Taishō ryōtei 常盤華壇. That tree runs to more than forty names — Iriya, Dōzaka, Namidabashi, Musashino, Akabane, Kappabashi, Kameido, Kameari, Sugamo Kōshinzuka, Kinshichō, Ohanajaya, Komagome, Toyosu — most of which are now independent shops with the same name and no shared ownership, which is why Tabelog lists a dozen unrelated ときわ食堂 across Tokyo. The Asakusa house is the one two doors from Kaminarimon, next to the crackers shop, on the most-photographed hundred metres in the city, and it has stayed a shokudō rather than becoming a tourist restaurant. Fuji TV's documentary strand ザ・ノンフィクション once filmed the succession here as a family argument: the fourth generation had been a management consultant before coming home, the third generation had spent his life watching customers' faces, and the line the son remembered from his father was 「お前には心がない」 — you have no heart. The fourth generation, 牧信真, is now the owner and president and has become one of the neighbourhood's public faces, appearing on Asakusa radio and food-walk events alongside the heirs of Yoshikami and Daikokuya. The kitchen's habit is 割烹技術を用いた和定食 — kappō technique applied to set meals — and the house's own slogan for what it does is smaller than that: 「日常をちょっと豊かに」, make ordinary days a little richer. It opens at 9:30 on weekdays and 8:30 at weekends, which in Asakusa means breakfast, and the aji fry is cut from wild horse mackerel the owner picks himself, so the price moves with the market. Thirty-six seats; expect to share a table when it is busy — 「混雑している場合は相席をお願いすることがあります」. It passed its centenary in 2022.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「日常をちょっと豊かに」 — make ordinary days a little richer. And the third generation's rebuke to the fourth, which the shop has never quite stopped answering: a business run only on numbers has no heart.
chef_bio.specialty: 名物 天然あじフライ ¥1,080 (wild horse mackerel, picked by the owner, price varies with the catch); かつ丼 ¥1,680; とんかつ定食 ¥1,880; まぐろ刺身定食 ¥1,880; 銀だら照焼 ¥1,500; 豆腐ステーキ with the house's inherited tare ¥980; 鍋焼きうどん ¥1,200; four soups — みそ汁 ¥280, なめこ汁 ¥330, 貝汁 ¥380, とん汁 ¥380

anecdotes.text: The menu prints the shop's own family tree of forty-plus Tokiwa Shokudō branches, from 料亭 常盤華壇 and the sōhonten down through Iriya, Namidabashi, Kameido, Sugamo Kōshinzuka, Kinshichō and Toyosu.
The succession was televised: Fuji TV's ザ・ノンフィクション followed the third-generation owner and his consultant son, and the line that stuck was the father's 「お前には心がない」 — you have no heart.
The horse mackerel is chosen by the owner himself and the price moves with it: 「当店のアジは、店主が目利きした天然アジを使用しており、仕入状況により価格が変わる場合がございます」.
Its own catchphrase for itself is 「気軽な和食屋」 — a Japanese place you can walk into without thinking about it.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The shop's own site publishes the complete menu with tax-inclusive prices in vertical script, the 1922 founding as the fifth branch of the Tokiwa Shokudō main house at Honjo Koume Narihira-chō, the forty-plus-branch family tree, the service policy 「日常をちょっと豊かに」, the trading hours (平日・土 9:30–22:00, 日祝 8:30–22:00, L.O. 21:30, 水曜 不定期休), the shared-table notice, the wild-aji sourcing note and — importantly — the open allergy invitation 「食材でアレルギーがある方は御遠慮なく（お申し出）して下さい」. Tabelog 13039346 independently confirms the address 浅草1-3-3, the phone 03-3847-8845, 36 seats, the ¥1,000–¥1,999 band, the Wednesday closure and the two-doors-from-Kaminarimon position, and dates the founding to 大正11年. A 2010 local feature by the Ueno-Asakusa guide network records the Fuji TV documentary, the third-to-fourth-generation succession and the shop's 「気軽な和食屋」 self-description; multiple later Japanese sources name the fourth-generation owner as 牧信真 and the operating company as 株式会社ときわ.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A single 36-seat shokudō kitchen with a fryer running all day for とんかつ, あじフライ, ハムカツ, 鶏の唐揚げ and ニンニク丸揚げ, plus a 鍋焼きうどん on the menu. Nothing is separated.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Wheat soy sauce is the default table condiment and the base of the 特製ダレ on the tofu steak and the 自家製照りダレ on the silver cod. The miso soups — a blended miso and a red miso — have not been specified, and 麦味噌 (barley miso) is common in shops of this type, so both need to be asked about.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The soups and the おひたし dressing are almost certainly dashi-based, and the fryer, the grill and the boards handle pork and fish continuously. A vegan plate here is rice, pickles, natto, nori and vegetables ordered around the kitchen rather than from it.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop prints an unprompted invitation on its own menu: 「食材でアレルギーがある方は御遠慮なく（お申し出）して下さい」 — please tell us without hesitation if you have a food allergy. That is a willingness to be asked, not a demonstrated coeliac protocol, but it is more than any other record in this shard offers.

positives.text: Several dishes never meet flour at all: 刺身盛合 ¥1,680, まぐろ刺身 ¥1,080, にしん塩焼 ¥1,500, さば塩焼 ¥880, plain rice ¥330 and お新香 ¥430. Salt-grilled fish and rice is a real meal for someone avoiding wheat, subject to the soy-sauce and miso questions.
The menu is printed with every price, tax included, and the daily specials are on a board — you can see the whole kitchen before you order.
Four different soups can be swapped into any set meal (とん汁 or 貝汁 +¥100, なめこ汁 +¥50), which makes it possible to steer around one you cannot have.

cultural_comfort.note: Two doors from Kaminarimon on the busiest tourist street in Tokyo, and still an ordinary neighbourhood canteen: 36 seats, prices printed in vertical Japanese script on a paper menu, a daily board on the wall, and a request that you share a table when it is full. No English menu was found in any source, but almost everything is a recognisable set meal and the shop is used to visitors — it opens at 9:30 on weekdays and 8:30 at weekends, which makes it one of the very few honest breakfasts near Sensō-ji. Closed Wednesdays, though the shop's own menu says the closure is irregular, so check before a Wednesday trip. The one line worth memorising before you go in is the shop's own: 「アレルギーがあります」 — they have printed on their menu that they want to hear it.
